title: Information-theoretic analysis of archived FLY-SURFER artifacts
guardrails: Mutual information does not establish causation.
Information about a label does not establish biological perception.
Neural decoding does not prove the brain uses that information.
Structural connectivity does not establish physiological information flow.
Direct stimulation responses are not downstream activity.
Phase 5 weight changes are not evidence of learning without behavioural evidence.
Deterministic repeats are never treated as independent replicates.
No gameplay label or ground truth was fabricated.

A_sensory_population.interpretation: The four-neuron response is a deterministic one-to-one function of distance in every archived mapping seed. The plug-in estimate is therefore log2(3) by construction. It checks the declared encoding; it is not a statistical discovery, and three mapping seeds cannot support a confirmatory claim.
A_sensory_population.replication_note: The block permutation treats each mapping seed as one cluster. With three clusters of three distances the null has exactly 6^3 = 216 within-seed assignments and is enumerated exactly. The observed bijection is reproduced only by the six permutations applied consistently to all three clusters, so the exact p is 6/216 ~ 0.028.
A_sensory_population.bootstrap_note: The cluster bootstrap interval collapses to the point estimate because all three mapping seeds produce the identical response. It reflects zero observed between-seed variation and is not a measure of precision.

A_population_sweep.label: population_size_sensitivity
A_population_sweep.observational_unit: one simulation run per distance per population size (15 runs); all groups share one mapping seed
A_population_sweep.interpretation: The joint distance code stays at log2(3) bits at every population size. Single-neuron estimates sum far above the joint estimate because each active neuron repeats the same distance identity. The split is descriptive: the plug-in bias is positive and the summed term double-counts shared information.
A_population_sweep.note: all groups share one mapping seed; this sweep is a descriptive sensitivity analysis, not an independent replication

caveats: A weight change is the output of the declared three-factor rule; it is not evidence of biological synaptic plasticity or learning.
Each per-seed table has 40 observations in 16 cells; its analytic MI bias floor is 0.1623 bits. The paired difference removes the first-order bias but not the sampling variance.
Ten seeds is the minimum declared for a confirmatory contrast; the exact sign-flip test over ten pairs cannot report p below 0.002.

C_reward_ablation.power_note: With three paired replicates the exact two-sided sign-flip test has eight assignments and cannot report p below 0.25. No significance claim is possible from this ablation.
caveats: A, C and F produce identical chosen actions in every replicate, so their contrasts with B coincide and are not independent evidence.

D_neural_motor.circularity: The Phase 4F decoder thresholds the same pool activity used as the predictor. The estimate is an internal-consistency check of a computational map, not evidence that the brain transmits motor commands.
D_neural_motor.interpretation: The decoder declares a state from thresholds on the same pool activity used as the predictor. High mutual information is expected and confirms that the decoder is internally consistent. It is not evidence that the brain transmits motor commands, and the sequential windows inside a run are not independent trials.

unavailable.status: at least one endpoint is unavailable

entries.label: real_replay_sensory_to_neural_mi
entries.reason: The Phase 3B2C replay persists aggregate spike counts only. No per-neuron or per-frame spike arrays were written, so a sensory-event to neural-response table cannot be formed without re-running the simulation.

entries.label: spike_train_entropy
entries.reason: No archived research run persists raw spike times at a scale that supports a per-neuron spike-train entropy estimate. The stored raw-spike arrays are a 1,564-spike initial run over 800 neurons, a 74-spike propagation smoke test and a Phase 3C.5 pilot with 64-72 spikes per condition. These are single trials with at most a few spikes per neuron.

entries.label: membrane_potential_entropy
entries.reason: Membrane potentials were never persisted by any phase.

entries.label: neural_level_plasticity_information
entries.reason: The Phase 5 real-BANC demonstration stores six named conditions but only three distinct spike hashes, five sequential 50 ms decoder windows per condition and the same decoded-state sequence in every condition. The repeated run is deterministic, not an independent replicate, so a neural-level baseline-versus-plastic information comparison cannot be given uncertainty.

entries.label: neural_level_reward_modulation
entries.reason: Reward providers are recorded for the Phase 5 real-BANC conditions, but those conditions share one decoded-state sequence and differ only by a deterministic repeat. No arm persists independent per-neuron activity, so a neural-level reward-modulation effect on information transmission is not estimable.

entries.label: cue_to_neural_response
entries.reason: In every archived Phase 5E and Phase 5F episode the per-episode cue spike count is the constant 8 and the total spike count is 12 (11 or 12 in condition E). A constant neural response cannot carry information about the cue.
